Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important run chase. The White Ferns are seen in a huddle as the umpires make their way onto the field. The opening duo for India Women, Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma are out in the middle as the players of New Zealand Women take their places on the field. Jess Kerr will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, New Zealand will be happy with where they are at in the game at the halfway mark. They have the momentum with them and will look to take this into their bowling effort as they aim to strike early. On the other hand, India will be hoping to replicate New Zealand's start by aiming for a steady and ideally, a wicket-less Powerplay. A strong foundation at the top will be crucial if they are to chase down the target. The dew didn’t  come in during the latter half of New Zealand’s innings, but it remains to be seen if it plays a role during India’s chase. Back in a bit for the run chase!

Georgia Plimmer is up for a flash interview. She begins by saying that they knew the pitches here would be low and slow and hence they wanted to go hard in the Powerplay. Is pretty happy with the total they have put on the board. Adds that she tried to stick to her natural game and was constantly having a chat with Bates. Ends by saying that it will be challenging to defend against a strong Indian line-up but they will try their best to prevent them from chasing.

Kerr couldn't add anything to her score after the incident, but Devine sensed the need to accelerate and took charge. The New Zealand skipper shifted gears brilliantly, unleashing a powerful assault on the Indian bowlers. Brooke Halliday chipped in with a handy knock as well. Adding to India’s woes, a slow over-rate penalty meant they were restricted to having one fielder fewer outside the 30-yard circle during the final over, which further aided the White Ferns.

Through the twin strikes, India were allowed to gain some control in the game and bring the scoring rate down. Tasked with a rebuild, Melie Kerr and Sophie Devine found it tough to get the Indian spinners away in the middle phase. An incident that is going to be talked about for a long time unfolded when Kerr attempted to sneak in a second run and found herself short of the crease. As she set off for the second, the umpire had already handed over her cap to the bowler, resulting in the over being called and Kerr getting a reprieve.

New Zealand Women get the desired final push, thanks to their skipper Sophie Devine! 37 runs came off the last three overs which has allowed the White Ferns to finish with 160 on the board. Earlier, after opting to bat first, New Zealand were off to a brisk start. Through their proactive approach, Suzie Bates and Georgia Plimmer were able to put the Indian bowlers under the pump in the Powerplay. When Ghosh dropped Bates on 18, danger loomed large for the Indians as the White Ferns built a strong foundation with a 55-run Powerplay.

Just a single to end but New Zealand Women will be happy with that effort. Shreyanka Patil flights the ball up around off, Sophie Devine sits down to fetch and slog it away over mid-wicket but miscues it badly. The ball gets skewed in front of short third and the batters get across for a single. New Zealand Women finish with 160/4 on the board!

Oh, deary me! What happened here? A lot of confusion in the middle as the Indian players feel Melie Kerr is run out here and she starts walking back as well but the umpires have deemed it as a dead ball. Coming to the delivery, it was bowled short around off, Kerr chopped it into long off for one. Harmanpreet Kaur seemed to be just walking in with the ball as it's the end of the over but the batters tried to sneak in an extra run while the umpire was handing the bowler her cap. Kaur throws the ball to Richa Ghosh and the bails are dislodged with Kerr nowhere in the frame but the umpires decide it's a dead ball after the single was taken. The decision is concrete but the Indian players and coaching staff aren't happy and the fourth umpire is now trying to calm things down. Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to get the play underway. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of India Women. It will be the duo of Suzie Bates and Georgia Plimmer to open the batting for New Zealand Women. Pooja Vastrakar has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

The start of the game isn't far away now and the match officials are out on the field. They are followed by the players of the two sides along with the mascots and the players will now line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of New Zealand first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Nasser Hussain is near the deck. He says that it has cooled down as compared to the first game of the day and the temperatures will be around 31 degrees. States that the square boundaries are 53 metres and 63 metres with the straight boundary being 73 metres long. WV Raman agrees with Nasser that the slight breeze blowing across will mean that dew is unlikely to set in. Looking at the grass coverage, Raman opines that there will be moderate pace and bounce and it could turn later on in the game.

Harmanpreet Kaur, the captain of India Women says that batting first or second doesn't matter much and they just want to go out there and play cricket. Adds that this group of players is fearless and they aren't afraid of taking the aggressive options. Mentions that they have a balanced side with three pacers and a deep batting lineup as well.

Sophie Devine, the captain of New Zealand Women says it looks like a good fresh surface and they want to put runs on the board. Says that the preparations have been good and they have trained well for the competition. Mentions that results haven't gone in their favour recently but they are always learning and moving on. States they have a balanced side and a long batting line-up too. Ends by saying it is all about a clean slate and putting your best foot forward.
New Zealand Women (Playing XI) - Suzie Bates, Georgia Plimmer, Melie Kerr, Sophie Devine (C), Brooke Halliday, Maddy Green, Izzy Gaze (WK), Jess Kerr, Rosemary Mair, Lea Tahuhu, Eden Carson.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Pooja Vastrakar, Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil, Asha Sobhana, Renuka Singh Thakur.
TOSS - New Zealand Women have won the toss and they will BAT first.

New Zealand Women on the other hand have been considered as the team that have the ability to break the Aussie-English dominance but the two-time finalists haven't quite been able to stay in touching distance with those at the top. The likes of Sophie Devine and Suzie Bates are still going and Melie Kerr gives them that genuine all-rounder in the middle of both innings. They do, however, need to start putting in better performances as a team if they are to go all the way. A fascinating encounter on the cards but only one team can walk away with two points. Who will it be? Only time will tell. Toss and team news in a bit.

India Women have shown a lot of promise in the last few years and have really emerged as the ones who can break the Aussie-English dominance when it comes to winning the big tournaments. However, they haven't really been able to get over the line and skipper Harmanpreet Kaur will be eyeing up that coveted title that eludes her side. They have a well-balanced side but that top order needs to fire if they are to go deep in the tournament.

Hello and a warm welcome to one and all! The 2024 edition of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup has kicked off in style in the UAE and it is now time for the second game on Day 2. India Women will be taking on New Zealand Women in Dubai in a Group A clash that should be a high-octane clash and a win here could be really crucial given how this group is set up.
... MATCH DAY ...

It's time for Group A action of the 2024 ICC Women's T20 World Cup to take centre stage at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium as India take on New Zealand. Placed in Group A alongside Australia, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka, this group is undoubtedly the 'Group of Death'. A loss for either side will put them under pressure early in the tournament, a scenario both teams will want to avoid. Therefore, it will be crucial for them to hit the ground running and set the tone for their respective World Cup campaigns. The White Ferns have endured a challenging 2024 in the format, with only one win from 13 matches heading into the World Cup. After their disappointing group-stage exit in the 2023 edition in South Africa, New Zealand’s goal will be to clear that hurdle this time around but will be focused on taking it one game at a time. The team has opted for continuity, retaining a core of experienced players from the 2023 edition in South Africa. As always, much of their success will depend on their all-rounder trio of Melie Kerr, Suzie Bates, and captain Sophie Devine, who will need to deliver if New Zealand are to make a deep run in the tournament. The team's recent form with the bat has been underwhelming, often leaving too much for the bowlers to do. Players like Georgia Plimmer, Maddy Green, and Brooke Halliday will need to step up and provide solid contributions to ease the pressure on the big names. On the bowling front, veteran Lea Tahuhu will spearhead the pace attack, backed by Rosemary Mair, Molly Penfold, Jess Kerr, and Hannah Rowe. Jess’s younger sister, Melie Kerr, will lead the spin department, with Fran Jonas, Eden Carson, and Leigh Kasperek rounding out the spin options. New Zealand boast a well-rounded bowling lineup capable of adapting to the various challenges they will encounter during the World Cup. As for India, after a smooth run during much of the Asia Cup in July, they faced a reality check in the final, where Sri Lanka defeated them. In the previous three editions of the Women's T20 World Cup, India have successfully navigated the group stage, finishing as runners-up in 2020 and reaching the semi-finals in the other two editions. The Women in Blue have been waiting a long time for an ICC trophy, much like their male counterparts before they finally broke the drought earlier this year. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur and her team will be hoping to replicate that success and go all the way. Although India won both their warm-up matches leading up to the event, their top three of Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana, and Harmanpreet Kaur did not perform as well as they would have liked, and they will be eager to hit the ground running. Jemimah Rodrigues, one of the better players of spin in the Indian setup, impressed with her contributions in both games and will be crucial in the middle overs, where spin is likely to dominate. Richa Ghosh and Deepti Sharma are expected to provide the late flourish with the presence of Yastika Bhatia and Dayalan Hemalatha adding depth to the batting unit. As always, India have opted for a spin-heavy approach for the World Cup, featuring Deepti Sharma, Shreyanka Patil, Radha Yadav, Asha Sobhana and Sajana Sajeevan as the options. In the pace department, Renuka Singh Thakur will lead the charge, supported by Pooja Vastrakar and Arundhati Reddy. With this balanced squad, India aim to make a strong impact in the tournament. Will India start their campaign with a win, or will New Zealand put their recent struggles behind them and secure a vital victory? We shall find out together.
